title: The Four Powers of Computational Thinking
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Computational Thinking
Decomposition
Pattern Recognition
Abstraction

Scratch
description: Interactive infographic with four clickable cards, one for each power of computational thinking: decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction and algorithm design. Clicking a card shows a one-sentence definition, a school-life example and a Scratch example, and a counter tracks how many powers the student has explored.

educational.topic: The four powers of computational thinking
learningObjectives: Given the name of one of the four powers of computational thinking, explain in your own words what that power means and give one everyday example of it.

controls.label: Decomposition, Pattern Recognition, Abstraction, Algorithm Design
controls.description: Click a card to select it and show its definition and examples

controls.label: Start Over
controls.description: Clears the selection and the explored counter

keyQuestions: What does each of the four powers mean in your own words?
Which power are you using when you notice that all four sides of a square are drawn the same way?
Can you think of a new everyday example for each power?
commonMisconceptions: Computational thinking means thinking like a robot. It is really the human work of making a problem clear enough for a computer to follow.
Abstraction removes the details. It only hides them behind a name.
assessmentOpportunities: Name a power and ask the student to explain it before clicking the card to check.
Ask the student for an everyday example that is not shown in the panel.
